symbols.name: triple set
symbols.meaning: The set of all three-element subsets of the ground set $[h]$, whose members are the triples.
symbols.quote: Let $\mathcal T$ be the set of all three-element subsets of $[h]$, whose members are *triples*.

symbols.name: triple of triples
symbols.meaning: A tuple of three triples, which indexes the entries of a bank.
symbols.quote: A *bank* is a family of scalars indexed by $\sigma=(\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3)\in\mathcal T^3$.

symbols.name: source vector
symbols.meaning: The vector, indexed by triples, of the entries of the source bank along the varying coordinate.
symbols.quote: For each invocation write $\xi$ for the source vector and $\eta$ for the target vector, so that $\xi_T$ and $\eta_S$ are their entries.

symbols.name: target vector
symbols.meaning: The vector, indexed by triples, of the entries of the target bank along the varying coordinate.
symbols.quote: For each invocation write $\xi$ for the source vector and $\eta$ for the target vector, so that $\xi_T$ and $\eta_S$ are their entries.

symbols.name: side wire
symbols.meaning: The scratch wire attached to an ordered neighbouring pair of triples $(S,T)$.
symbols.quote: Each ordered neighbouring pair $(S,T)$ has a *side wire* $A_{ST}$, and each $\ell\in[h]$ has a *central wire* $C_\ell$.

symbols.name: central wire
symbols.meaning: The scratch wire attached to the element $\ell$ of the ground set.
symbols.quote: Each ordered neighbouring pair $(S,T)$ has a *side wire* $A_{ST}$, and each $\ell\in[h]$ has a *central wire* $C_\ell$.

symbols.name: ground element
symbols.meaning: An element of the ground set $[h]$, which names one central wire.
symbols.quote: Each ordered neighbouring pair $(S,T)$ has a *side wire* $A_{ST}$, and each $\ell\in[h]$ has a *central wire* $C_\ell$.

symbols.name: label vector
symbols.meaning: A vector of the rational space $E$ on which the label form is defined.
symbols.quote: For the bit network take $E=\mathbb Q^h$ with the form $\langle\mathbf p,\mathbf q\rangle=\mathbf p^{\mathsf T}(I-J/9)\mathbf q$, where $\mathbf p,\mathbf q$ are vectors of $E$ and $J$ is the all-ones matrix.

symbols.name: second label vector
symbols.meaning: A second vector of the rational space $E$, paired with $\mathbf p$ by the label form.
symbols.quote: For the bit network take $E=\mathbb Q^h$ with the form $\langle\mathbf p,\mathbf q\rangle=\mathbf p^{\mathsf T}(I-J/9)\mathbf q$, where $\mathbf p,\mathbf q$ are vectors of $E$ and $J$ is the all-ones matrix.

symbols.name: dual space
symbols.meaning: The dual space of the smaller label $U'$, the space of linear functionals on $U'$.
symbols.quote: Edge residuals are computed through the [dual space](dual-space.md) $U'^{*}$, the linear functionals on $U'$.

relations.quote: The network labels its wires with [subspace labels](subspace-labels.md): nondegenerate subspaces of a fixed bilinear space $E$.

relations.predicate: is built within the framework of
relations.quote: The network is built within the framework of [Linear networks and frames](linear-network-frames.md): each wire is a role, and a common representation on the wires of a gate lets the gate act on arrays, pointwise.
The labels' orthogonality and nondegeneracy are tested with the [bilinear form](bilinear-form.md) of $E$.
Nondegeneracy is checked through the [eigenvalues](eigenvalue.md) of the form matrix $I-J/9$.
Edge residuals are computed through the [dual space](dual-space.md) $U'^{*}$, the linear functionals on $U'$.
